title: Lazy Student
statementMd:
Student Vladislav came to his programming exam completely unprepared as usual. He got a question about some strange algorithm on a graph — something that will definitely never be useful in real life. He asked a girl sitting next to him to lend him some cheat papers for this questions and found there the following definition:

*The minimum spanning tree* $*T*$ of graph $*G*$ is such a tree that it contains all the vertices of the original graph $*G*$, and the sum of the weights of its edges is the minimum possible among all such trees.

Vladislav drew a graph with $*n*$ vertices and $*m*$ edges containing no loops and multiple edges. He found one of its minimum spanning trees and then wrote for each edge its weight and whether it is included in the found tree or not. Unfortunately, the piece of paper where the graph was painted is gone and the teacher is getting very angry and demands to see the original graph. Help Vladislav come up with a graph so that the information about the minimum spanning tree remains correct.

## Input

The first line of the input contains two integers $*n*$ and $*m*$ (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ff8ab63d2234d30c36551ae9737f0ccd16b68b4c.png)) — the number of vertices and the number of edges in the graph.

Each of the next $*m*$ lines describes an edge of the graph and consists of two integers $*a*_{*j*}$ and $*b*_{*j*}$ ($1 ≤ *a*_{*j*} ≤ 10^{9}, *b*_{*j*} = {0, 1}$). The first of these numbers is the weight of the edge and the second number is equal to $1$ if this edge was included in the minimum spanning tree found by Vladislav, or $0$ if it was not.

It is guaranteed that exactly $*n* - 1$ number ${*b*_{*j*}}$ are equal to one and exactly $*m* - *n* + 1$ of them are equal to zero.

## Output

If Vladislav has made a mistake and such graph doesn't exist, print $- 1$.

Otherwise print $*m*$ lines. On the $*j*$-th line print a pair of vertices $(*u*_{*j*}, *v*_{*j*})$ ($1 ≤ *u*_{*j*}, *v*_{*j*} ≤ *n*, *u*_{*j*} ≠ *v*_{*j*}$), that should be connected by the $*j*$-th edge. The edges are numbered in the same order as in the input. The graph, determined by these edges, must be connected, contain no loops or multiple edges and its edges with $*b*_{*j*} = 1$ must define the minimum spanning tree. In case there are multiple possible solutions, print any of them.
statementZhMd:
<statement>

学生 Vladislav 像往常一样毫无准备地来参加编程考试。他遇到了一道关于图上某种奇怪算法的问题——这种东西在现实生活中肯定永远派不上用场。他向坐在旁边的女生借了一些这道题的小抄，并在上面找到了如下定义：

*图* $*G*$ 的*最小生成树* $*T*$ 是这样一棵树：它包含原图 $*G*$ 的所有顶点，并且在所有满足条件的树中，其边权之和尽可能小。

Vladislav 画出了一个包含 $*n*$ 个顶点和 $*m*$ 条边、没有自环和重边的图。他找到了其中一棵最小生成树，然后记录了每条边的权值，以及该边是否包含在找到的树中。不幸的是，画有图的纸张丢失了，而老师越来越生气，要求他展示原图。请帮助 Vladislav 构造一个图，使得关于最小生成树的信息仍然正确。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个整数 $*n*$ 和 $*m*$ (![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ff8ab63d2234d30c36551ae9737f0ccd16b68b4c.png))，表示图中的顶点数和边数。

接下来的 $*m*$ 行中的每一行描述图的一条边，包含两个整数 $*a*_{*j*}$ 和 $*b*_{*j*}$（$1 ≤ *a*_{*j*} ≤ 10^{9}, *b*_{*j*} = {0, 1}$）。其中，第一个数是边的权值；如果该边包含在 Vladislav 找到的最小生成树中，则第二个数等于 $1$，否则等于 $0$。

保证恰好有 $*n*$ - 1 个 ${*b*_{*j*}}$ 等于 one，并且恰好有 $*m*$ - $*n*$ + 1 个等于 zero。

## 输出格式

如果 Vladislav 犯了错，不存在这样的图，则输出 $- 1$。

否则，输出 $*m*$ 行。第 $*j*$ 行输出一对顶点 $(*u*_{*j*}, *v*_{*j*})$（$1 ≤ *u*_{*j*}, *v*_{*j*} ≤ *n*, *u*_{*j*} ≠ *v*_{*j*}$），表示第 $*j*$ 条边应连接的两个顶点。边的编号与输入中的顺序相同。由这些边确定的图必须是连通的，不包含自环或重边，并且其中 $b*_{*j*} = 1$ 的边必须构成最小生成树。如果有多种可能的解，输出任意一种即可。

</statement>
